beats.role_note: COLD OPEN LAW — Claude UI, ask lands answered; introduces Liam in for Bear
beats.narration_text: Hej, this is Liam, in for Bear. Today we tear down the skill that made this video — ai-explainer. It's the one you point Claude at when you want the Brutalist Claude cut: cream page, warm ink, one terracotta accent, a real narrator, and a whole workflow that reads a SKILL file end to end before it draws a single frame. Here's how it actually works.

beats.role_note: EXECUTIVE-SUMMARY LAW — hesitant writer corrects the reel's actual misconception into its claim
beats.narration_text: The easy mistake is to call this skill a template pack. It isn't. It's a workflow that reads a whole SKILL file, sets the brand and voice, drives every phase, and refuses to publish. When you ask for the Claude cut, this is the file Claude opens first.

props.text:
The ai-explainer skill
is a template.
It reads a whole SKILL file first.

beats.role_note: FRAMEWORK-FIRST — what a skill IS, before the pipeline. Anatomy of the ai-explainer folder.
beats.narration_text: A skill is a folder. A SKILL file at the top — the doctrine Claude reads before doing anything — and the files it references. For ai-explainer, that means the register prose, the brand file, the outro lock, the pipeline safety notes, and the parent explainer chassis it extends. The instructions govern; the code just executes them.

props.title: A skill is a folder Claude reads first.
props.calloutText: The SKILL.md is the instruction. Claude opens it, reads every referenced file, then works.

beats.role_note: The pipeline — phases and contracts, source: SKILL.md §Flow
beats.narration_text: The skill runs one pipeline, always in the same order. Scaffold the folder and brand metadata. Write narration in the Teardown register. Generate the voice locally with Kokoro — that's the clock. Fill each beat's visual slot from Remotion scenes, Manim fragments, or Onda code blocks. Then compile to a four K master beside the reel. Never uploads. Never publishes.

props.title: One pipeline, five phases, one master.
props.footerNote: Audio-first. Every visual conforms to the measured voice.
props.sparkLine: The voice measures. Everything else conforms.

beats.role_note: Design decision 1 — the fixed bookend spine. Cold open, BLUF, body, verdict, handoff, outro.
beats.narration_text: The first design decision is the shape of every reel. Cold open on the Claude composer. Beat two is a hesitant writer, correcting a real misconception into the reel's actual claim. The body illustrates. The verdict is an artifact card. The handoff types a paste-ready prompt. The outro restates the title. Same six moves, every episode.

props.heading: Fixed bookends. Free interior.
props.body: Cold open · BLUF · body · verdict · handoff · outro. Six moves in the same order every time — so the middle can be anything the concept needs.
props.quote: The bookends do not change… The modifier governs the MIDDLE.

beats.role_note: Design decision 2 — ILLUSTRATE LAW. Anti-wallpaper: the UI earns its beats.
beats.narration_text: Second decision. The Claude interface only appears where the interface is the subject — cold open, ask beats, verdict, handoff, outro. Every other beat has to ILLUSTRATE its concept: a diagram, a Manim fragment, an Onda code block, a Remotion illustration. Two composer beats in a row is the smell. Seven videos of composer wallpaper is the failure this law exists to prevent.

props.heading: The UI earns its beats.
props.body: Composer only where the composer IS the subject. Every other beat illustrates the concept — diagram, Manim, code block, custom illustration.
props.quote: Two consecutive beats sharing the same visual scheme is the smell; seven videos of composer wallpaper is the failure this law exists to prevent.

beats.role_note: Design decision 3 — ASK→RESULT LAW. The signature receipt move.
beats.narration_text: Third decision. Whenever the reel is about to show a generated visual, it first shows the Claude prompt that made it. Composer beat with the ACTUAL prompt typed in, then the graphic. Never a rendered chart alone — always the ask, then the receipt. That habit is why this brand feels like the tool it's teaching, not a slideshow about it.

props.heading: Ask, then the receipt.
props.body: Every generated graphic is preceded by the composer showing the actual prompt that made it. The Claude UI is the receipt — never decoration.
props.quote: The Claude interface is never shown alone as decoration — it is always followed by what it produced. Ask beats stay in the fixed Claude skin; RESULT graphics render in the episode's CHANNEL palette.

beats.role_note: The design tell — where it bites. The Teardown honest judgment. Falsifiability beat.
beats.narration_text: Here's where the skill bites. The instructions govern everything, which means an unread paragraph is a silent bug — a stale outro handle, a missing Beat two, a wallpaper reel. The lint helps, but the discipline is human. And Liam is a named substitute, never a Bear clone. If a reel needs Bear's voice, you rebuild it on the Bear channel. That's a one-variable change, not a re-authoring — but it IS a change, and the skill will not fake it.

props.heading: Where it bites.
props.body: The doctrine is only enforced if the operator READS it. An unread rule ships as a bug. And Liam is a named substitute — never a Bear clone.
props.quote: A named voice, never a clone. Liam does not imitate Bear's delivery or claim to be him.
props.sparkLine: The instructions still need a reader.

beats.role_note: VERDICT — artifact card. Recapitulates what the skill IS.
beats.narration_text: The verdict. ai-explainer is the SKILL that turns a topic into a Brutalist Claude reel — cream page, warm ink, one terracotta accent, real narration, and a spine you can teach. It reads the whole doctrine before it draws. It illustrates the middle. It never publishes.

artifactLines: A workflow, not a template pack.
The UI earns every beat (ILLUSTRATE LAW).
Kokoro is the clock. compile.py conforms.

beats.role_note: HANDOFF LAW — Your Turn composer with a paste-ready prompt Liam reads aloud.
beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude Code inside a cloned Brutalist toolkit: use the ai-explainer skill to build a two-hundred-second reel about a concept in your field, with the Liam voice — Kokoro am_onyx — the Humanitarians AI handle, no captions, and no publish step. Then check: does the middle illustrate, not wallpaper? Does every generated visual land after its ask? If both hold, the skill did its job.
